## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A seven-*juan* mid-Qīng (Qiánlóng-era) running subcommentary on the Lotus Sūtra by Dátiān Tōnglǐ 達天通理 (1701–1782), the principal mid-Qīng Beijing Buddhist scholar and *Chǎnjiào Chánshī* 闡教禪師. The principal substantive volume of the four-text *Zhǐzhǎng shū* complex ([KR6d0095](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0095) sectional analysis; [KR6d0096](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0096) introductory exposition; [KR6d0097](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0097) main commentary; [KR6d0098](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0098) matters-and-meanings glossary). The genre title *zhǐzhǎng* 指掌 ("pointing-the-palm") indicates a commentary intended to make the Lotus Sūtra's meaning as clear as if pointing to one's own palm.

**Abstract**

Tōnglǐ's *Zhǐzhǎng shū* is the most ambitious mid-Qiánlóng Lotus Sūtra commentary outside the imperial *Lóngzàng* canon project. The work draws on the Tiāntái commentarial tradition ([智顗](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E9%A1%97) Zhìyǐ's *Wénjù* [KR6d0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0014), [湛然](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B9%9B%E7%84%B6) Zhànrán's *Wénjù jì* [KR6d0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0015)), the late-Míng synthetic apparatus of [德清](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BE%B7%E6%B8%85) Hānshān Déqīng and [智旭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E6%97%AD) Ǒuyì Zhìxù, and the early-Qīng compendia of [智祥](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E7%A5%A5) Zhìxiáng ([KR6d0089](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0089)) and [大義](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A4%A7%E7%BE%A9) Dàyì ([KR6d0085](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0085)), synthesising these into a definitive Qiánlóng-era exposition.

Tōnglǐ was the most institutionally significant Beijing Buddhist scholar of the mid-Qīng. He was *Chǎnjiào Chánshī* under Qiánlóng imperial appointment and was responsible for the systematic Buddhist instructional curriculum of the high-Qiánlóng court. His four-text *Zhǐzhǎng shū* complex represents the institutional culmination of mid-Qīng Buddhist scholastic productive activity at the Beijing imperial court.

The dating is bracketed within Tōnglǐ's mature productive period c. 1750–1782; the four-text complex was probably completed in the 1770s, after the major imperial canon project of the *Lóngzàng* (1738) had been completed and after Tōnglǐ had achieved his mature institutional position.
